item.content:encoded:
I like this overall and I like a lot of the ideas in it but I can't really bring myself to upvote it.

I think a big issue with the article is that it fails to sell the sense of scale it's going for.

+ show block
– hide block

I don't buy that Foundation documents from thousands of years in the future are going to be so recognisable and so similar to what we're used to. SEEK discovers multiple other intelligent civilisations which have all existed and died fairly recently, but TOME still focuses largely on humanity, even though that's billions and billions of years for other species and civilisations to have arisen.

I love the idea of the Solitary Conceptual Bunker: forcing some inhuman force into a human sized hole to make it killable, that's a great idea. But it's an idea that I think would work far better with a smaller SCP. The Black Moon is just built up to be *so* large that, as clever as the way of defeating it is, it can't help but feel underwhelming that the final fate of reality just comes down to a fist fight. It's again a problem with a sense of scale that the SCP tries to cultivate but the delivery doesn't do justice. On top of that, The Administrator just seems too goofy and go lucky for a guy who has been trapped in isolation in a theoretical bar for billions (or, more likely, trillions) of years. The very final ending of him restarting the universe is a grandiose, optimistic note but one that doesn't feel earned: I don't feel like there's enough struggle or foreshadowing in the previous offsets to justify this final victory.

While I appreciate a mystery and not wanting to overexplain things I also think that too little about the nature of the Black Moon and the Counterbalance are revealed for the reader to feel properly invested in their struggle.

At first I wasn't sure if I liked the 173 reference, but after rereading it I think it and the idea behind KEY really works.

Definitely not going to downvote this because it is good, but it's not as good as it could be.

item.content:encoded:
Very interesting. Despite my abject hatred for most of the tropes introduced in the first two documents, you managed to make me enjoy the article. It was a gripping read.

The progression of the "Does the Black Moon howl?" questions was cool, how they thematically linked to the offset they were on and how the answers kept increasing in severity.

+ Things I'd like to point out
– hide block

SCP-001-CAGE has claimed that it is a result of being designated as 'the Counterbalance'

Should be "a being"

was discovered on a planet which it has identified as 'Grlern'

My name is a sequence of lights and movements your body configuration is not capable of.

Why would it have a verbal name for its planet while its communication is telepathic and its naming system is gestural?

There's … it's … it's taking people everyday!

"Every day" looks a lot more clinical/just better, in my eyes.

Visually, it resembles a bar

As much as I like this scene… why a bar? This dude is older than the Paleolithic, why would he pick a place from the last 50 or so years of our modern history when he's been around from the invention of the name to its obsoletion?

Just fucking die already!

As Mikaelious above said, this takes me out of the scene pretty hard.

Let there be light

Cheesy.

+1.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A wonderful story and concept from start to finish. I have to admit though, I almost wish that we had gotten a bit more time with the Administrator-the series of intermissions throughout the piece begs for some more character development from the Administrator, who is such a good character that I think you could do with some more action featuring them.

Additionally, the last page is a delight to read, but I almost think that the Black Moon could use just a tad more fleshing out-the problem with having a dark mysterious force for most of a long epic is that we just don't get enough appreciation for his malevolence until right towards the end. For the first few chapters, the Black Moon is so minor that it seems to take a backstage to the action of the rest of the story, and the ramping up of obliterations happens a bit too suddenly for me-it wasn't apparent in the middle chapters at how quickly the Black Moon was now causing obliterations, which made the end a bit more jarring-it took me a moment to realize that the Black Moon had progressed to full on universal level annihilation.

However, these are all relatively minor quibbles for what is a really great piece. It's a tough task to create entirely new characters with cosmic importance, give them personality, and make us care about their struggles over the course of a single SCP, and you've done a stellar job here.

I’m very torn on this piece.

The last two bits are phenomenal, especially the script-like section at the very end. However everything up until the Fungus entity is a bit of a slog to get through and I struggle taking it wholly seriously.

The Administrator as a character also lacks a cohesive voice throughout the story IMO. He comes off way more self-serious in the first sections before becoming a lot more fun towards the end. The last part reminded me a lot of David Tennant’s 10th Doctor in the best way possible.

I’m going to novote on this one. It’s got some awesome parts but the opening chapters make it hard for me to upvote.
